EV Infrastructure Analysis - Modeling

import libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
library(Hmisc)
library(ggplot2)
library(randomForest)

import data from preprocessing

ev_data_by_state <- read_csv("data/ev_data_by_state.csv")
ev_data_by_state

ev_stations_locations <- read_csv("data/ev_station_locations.csv")
ev_stations_locations

set random seed

set.seed(42)

predictive linear modeling based on registrations and population goal: predict the number of stations that each state should have based on registration count and population

model_lm = lm(total_stations ~ registration_count + population, data = ev_data_by_state)
summary(model_lm)

Call:
lm(formula = total_stations ~ registration_count + population, 
    data = ev_data_by_state)

Residuals:
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-1031.5  -204.5  -102.7   123.2  2277.3 

Coefficients:
                    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)        1.881e+02  1.134e+02   1.659 0.103750    
registration_count 1.184e-02  7.525e-04  15.734  < 2e-16 ***
population         6.699e-05  1.821e-05   3.679 0.000602 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

Residual standard error: 547.3 on 47 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.9578,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.956 
F-statistic: 533.6 on 2 and 47 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

predict stations based on model expected stations = stations the model predicts should exist in each state based solely on registrations and population station gap = difference between expected stations and current stations

ev_data_by_state_model <- ev_data_by_state |>
  rename(ev_stations = total_stations,
         ev_registrations = registration_count) |>
  mutate(expected_stations = round(predict(model_lm), 0),
         station_gap = expected_stations - ev_stations) |>
  arrange(desc(station_gap))
ev_data_by_state_model

visualize station gap from linear model

plot_usmap(data = ev_data_by_state_model, values = "station_gap", color = "white") + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red",
    midpoint = 0, name = "Station Gap"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "EV Charging Station Gaps by State (LM w/ Registration + Population)",
    subtitle = "Red = Underbuilt, Blue = Overbuilt"
  )

ggsave("outputs/modeling/ev_charging_station_gaps_by_state_1.png", bg = "skyblue")

ev_data_by_state_model_10 <- ev_data_by_state_model |>
  head(10)

ggplot(ev_data_by_state_model_10, aes(x = reorder(state, -station_gap), y = station_gap)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Underbuilt EV States (LM w/ Registration + Population)",
    x = "State",
    y = "Station Gap"
  ) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = station_gap), vjust = -0.2)

ggsave("outputs/modeling/top_10_underbuilt_states_1.png")

I believe it is a fair assumption to say that the average person does not worry about where to fuel up when driving an internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle. Unless driving in extremely rural areas, gas stations are readily available, have enough pumps, and experience minimal downtime. Let’s do a better job predicting how many EVs each state will need based on the current gasoline infrastructure.

Gas Station Data: https://afdc.energy.gov/files/u/data/data_source/10333/10333_gasoline_stations_year.xlsx

Caveat: data only through 2012 (historical trends show a decline in number of gas stations since 1996)

import and clean up data

gas_stations <- read.csv("data/2012_gas_stations_us.csv")

gas_stations <- gas_stations |>
  rename(gas_stations = X2012) |>
  rename(state = State)

gas_stations$state <- state.abb[match(gas_stations$state, state.name)]
gas_stations

join with state-level data for analysis

ev_gas_stations <- ev_data_by_state_model |>
  left_join(gas_stations) |>
  select(state, ev_stations, gas_stations) |>
  mutate(difference = gas_stations - ev_stations) |>
  arrange(desc(difference))
ev_gas_stations

according to this data, there are only three states with more EV stations than gas stations (CO, MA, CA) all other states have more gas stations than EV stations

goal: predict the number of EV stations each state needs but factor in the number of gas stations this time

join the datasets

ev_gas_full <- ev_gas_stations |>
  left_join(ev_data_by_state_model) |>
  select(-...1) |>
  arrange(desc(ev_stations))
ev_gas_full

implement the model

model_lm_gas = lm(ev_stations ~ ev_registrations + population + gas_stations, data = ev_gas_full)
summary(model_lm_gas)

Call:
lm(formula = ev_stations ~ ev_registrations + population + gas_stations, 
    data = ev_gas_full)

Residuals:
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-890.79 -218.42  -81.49  163.52 2244.45 

Coefficients:
                   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)       2.490e+02  1.186e+02   2.099  0.04132 *  
ev_registrations  1.107e-02  8.958e-04  12.358 3.21e-16 ***
population        1.178e-04  3.766e-05   3.127  0.00306 ** 
gas_stations     -1.097e-01  7.152e-02  -1.534  0.13184    
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

Residual standard error: 539.6 on 46 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.9599,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.9573 
F-statistic: 366.8 on 3 and 46 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

number of gas stations is not significant, so it most likely did not alter the model much

let’s look at the predictions from this model

ev_gas_predicted <- ev_gas_full |>
  mutate(expected_stations = round(predict(model_lm_gas), 0),
         station_gap = expected_stations - ev_stations) |>
  arrange(desc(station_gap))
ev_gas_predicted

visualize station gap from the new linear model with gas stations included

plot_usmap(data = ev_gas_predicted, values = "station_gap", color = "white") + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red",
    midpoint = 0, name = "Station Gap"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "EV Charging Station Gaps by State (LM w/ Registration + Population + Gas Stations)",
    subtitle = "Red = Underbuilt, Blue = Overbuilt"
  )

ggsave("outputs/modeling/ev_charging_station_gaps_by_state_2.png", bg = "skyblue")

factor in geographic area to the model

import state geographic data and convert to state abbreviations State Area Data: https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/2010/geo/state-area.html

state_areas <- read.csv("data/state_areas.csv")
state_areas$state <- state.abb[match(state_areas$state, state.name)]
state_areas

join with dataset

ev_gas_area <- ev_gas_full |>
  left_join(state_areas) |>
  arrange(desc(sq_mi))
ev_gas_area

create new linear model factoring in sq_miles (land area for each state) note: re-running other models with same dataset for analysis

model_lm_area <- lm(ev_stations ~ ev_registrations + population + sq_mi, data = ev_gas_area)
summary(model_lm_area)

Call:
lm(formula = ev_stations ~ ev_registrations + population + sq_mi, 
    data = ev_gas_area)

Residuals:
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-886.17 -197.12  -97.58  118.79 2217.06 

Coefficients:
                   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)       2.505e+02  1.257e+02   1.992 0.052349 .  
ev_registrations  1.189e-02  7.516e-04  15.821  < 2e-16 ***
population        6.753e-05  1.816e-05   3.718 0.000544 ***
sq_mi            -9.161e-04  8.093e-04  -1.132 0.263512    
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

Residual standard error: 545.7 on 46 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.959, Adjusted R-squared:  0.9563 
F-statistic: 358.3 on 3 and 46 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

visualize based on combination

ev_gas_area_predicted_lm<- ev_gas_area |>
  mutate(expected_stations = round(predict(model_lm_gas_area), 0),
         station_gap = expected_stations - ev_stations) |>
  arrange(desc(station_gap))
ev_gas_area_predicted_lm
plot_usmap(data = ev_gas_area_predicted_lm, values = "station_gap", color = "white") + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red",
    midpoint = 0, name = "Station Gap"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "EV Charging Station Gaps by State (LM w/ Registration + Population + Gas Stations + Area)",
    subtitle = "Red = Underbuilt, Blue = Overbuilt"
  )

ggsave("outputs/modeling/ev_charging_station_gaps_by_state_5.png", bg = "skyblue")

including area seemed to reduce the extremes (mainly, California)
